summary.headline: Federal Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 36.57% YoY to INR1,176.93 crores, with NIM at 3.33% and GNPA at 1.52%.
summary.overview: Federal Bank reported a strong Q1 FY27, with profit up 36.57% YoY on NII growth of 26.06% and NIM expansion of 13 bps QoQ to 3.33%, achieved with little treasury contribution. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.52%, NNPA at a record-low 0.18%, and fresh slippages down 37.8% YoY. CASA ratio rose 188 bps YoY to 32.23%, and management reiterated the mid-teens growth guidance with a positive bias. Management flagged the ECL transition from 1 April 2027, estimating a one-time impact of 1.5% to 2% of net worth, and noted a rising inflation and West Asia-linked fuel pass-through backdrop.

financial_highlights.change: up 13 bps QoQ, up 39 bps YoY
GNPA down 39 bps YoY; NNPA down 30 bps YoY
down 37.8% YoY, down 13.6% QoQ; slippage ratio 0.61%
balance up 18.26% YoY; ratio up 188 bps YoY

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: Grew 22.96% YoY; CV/CE book grew 21.07% YoY, with exposure focused on medium-sized fleet operators rather than single-truck operators.

segments.name: Corporate and Institutional Banking
segments.commentary: Grew 16.12% YoY but only about 6% QoQ; gross CIB book crossed INR1 lakh crores. Management called the quarterly pace opportunistic and not the normal trajectory.

segments.name: Retail banking
segments.commentary: Grew 10.8% YoY overall. Gold loans grew 33% YoY, cards 36% YoY, and loan against property 21% YoY; gold LTV is about 60%.

segments.name: Business banking
segments.commentary: Grew 7% YoY; slippages down 36% YoY. Management said growth will be pushed from here now that portfolio health is better.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: CA grew 18% YoY, SA 19.3% YoY, and FCNR(B) 37.76% YoY. Average SA cost is about 2.6%.

guidance_outlook: Loan growth guidance of mid-teens plus, with management stating a positive bias.
NIM expected to improve about 5-6 bps per quarter on average over the next 3-4 quarters, not necessarily linear.
ROA expected to improve about 3-4 bps per quarter, per prior guidance, with management reiterating it.
Credit cost: management indicated the lower end of the 50-60 bps guidance band, but did not formally revise it, citing war and monsoon headwinds.
ECL transition effective 1 April 2027: one-time impact of about 1.5% to 2% of net worth; no material ongoing P&L impact expected.
CASA ratio improvement target unchanged; LCR to be operated in the 115-120% range (Q1 average 117%).
capex_capacity: Standard Chartered India credit card portfolio acquisition in progress; integration targeted before end of calendar 2026.
Leverage-linked FCNR deposit product launched; some GIFT City IBU limits already allotted and more in pipeline.
Lines being arranged with offshore banks to channel leverage for customers directly.
Usual FCNR share of about 2.5%, per management's definition of fair share.
Obtained investment-grade international credit rating from S&P, opening access to bonds, ECBs and IBU funding.
demand_pricing: Cost of deposits fell about 11 bps QoQ excluding the Q4 reinvestment-deposit year-end interest effect; a further 2 bps came from IT refund interest and yield on advances fell 3 bps.
Mid-market shift: 75-80% of new corporate customer acquisition is now mid-market, with yield upticks reported.
Low-yield share of book rose to 50.1% from 49.8% QoQ, attributed to opportunistic short-term corporate lending.
Headline CPI averaged about 3.93% in Q1 and reached 4.38% in June; food inflation reached 5.32% in June; RBI repo held at 5.25%, FY27 GDP forecast cut to 6.6%, inflation forecast raised to 5.1%.
Management reported no meaningful stress yet in CV/CE or MSME books, though it is watching the fuel-price and monsoon impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did processing fees fall sequentially, and is NIM sustainable with cost of funds near bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: Processing fees are seasonally lower in Q1 than Q4 because disbursements vary. Management said NIM is supported by liability actions and asset-mix change, and that CASA momentum should persist.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 22 bps QoQ drop in cost of deposits, and is there more to come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 11 bps was the real reduction after excluding the year-end reinvestment-deposit effect, plus about 2 bps from IT refund interest, with yield on advances down 3 bps. Management said a little more deposit-cost relief remains in one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the CASA growth and its mix across retail, commercial and corporate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited doubling of current-account openings vs a year ago, KPI changes favouring liability-side work, and competitive products. CA growth was roughly equal across retail, commercial and corporate.

qa_highlights.question: Will the credit cost guidance be revised given Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 credit cost was 41 bps, is likely to be at the lower end of the 50-60 bps guidance, but is not formally revising it given war and monsoon headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FCNR window affect deposits and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FCNR target, saying it expects its fair share, usually about 2.5%. Cost comparison depends on swap rates, rupee rates and timing; leverage adds asset-side growth, so it is not treated as a deposit-cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the business loan and auto segment growth set to pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named auto and small business loans as segments needing sharper execution. It said auto was hit by internal reorganisation and business loans had risk-metric cleanup, and that guardrails are now in place to push growth.

risks_watch: ECL transition from 1 April 2027 with a one-time net worth hit of 1.5-2%.
Inflation rising to 4.38% in June with fuel pass-through and monsoon risk to MSME, CV/CE and gold-loan books.
Gold loan tonnage reportedly down about 10-11% YoY per an analyst's question; management did not dispute this, and LTV is about 60%.
Current-account seasonality in Q1 and the pace of CASA ratio improvement from 32.23%.
Auto segment underperformance and business loan growth pick-up dependent on execution.
Timing and pricing of FCNR and leverage-linked deposits and ECB/IBU borrowings, sensitive to swap and rupee rates.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's operating results and the mid-teens growth guidance with a positive bias, but cautious on credit costs and the macro backdrop, where management declined to formally revise guidance. Evasive on the FCNR cost-effectiveness and on the quantum of NIM upside beyond guidance.

We do now, and it is central to how we build the leverage this time.

growth.why: Management reiterated mid-teens-plus loan growth with a positive bias, backed by segment momentum (CV/CE +21%, gold +33%, cards +36%) and the Standard Chartered card portfolio acquisition, but gave no specific capacity or order numbers behind it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided NIM up about 5-6 bps per quarter on average over the next 3-4 quarters (Q1 NIM 3.33%, up 13 bps QoQ), backed by liability actions, lower cost of deposits (about 11 bps real QoQ cut) and asset-mix change; not necessarily linear.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Loan growth guided at mid-teens plus with a positive bias (gross advances up nearly 15% YoY, CV/CE +21%, gold +33%, cards +36%), plus the Standard Chartered card portfolio acquisition, though CIB growth was called opportunistic and business banking growth is yet to pick up.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is likely at the lower end of the 50-60 bps credit cost band (Q1 at 41 bps) and expects a positive bias on loan growth, but has not formally revised guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged war and monsoon headwinds, CPI at 4.38% in June, a cut to FY27 GDP forecast to 6.6%, and gold tonnage reportedly down about 10-11% YoY, none of which were disputed on the call.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Leverage-linked FCNR deposit product already launched with GIFT City IBU limits being allotted and more in the pipeline, and lines being arranged with offshore banks to channel leverage to customers.

rows.label: ECL transition from 1 April 2027
rows.why: One-time net worth impact of about 1.5% to 2% at transition, with management expecting no material ongoing P&L impact.

rows.label: Standard Chartered India credit card portfolio acquisition
rows.why: Acquisition is in progress and cards already grew 36% YoY, so it adds to card-book growth within the window.

rows.label: S&P investment-grade rating
rows.why: Opens access to bonds, ECBs and IBU funding, which gives the bank a new non-deposit funding channel to deploy.

oneOffs.what: Q4 reinvestment-deposit year-end interest effect and IT refund interest (about 2 bps) flattered the QoQ cost-of-deposit decline; not a growth item per se but a non-recurring benefit in the quarter

quality.why: Net profit rose 36.57% and NII 26.06% on a business-led basis with gross advances up nearly 15% and deposits up 11.37%, but the brief gives no quantified one-off that inflates YoY growth; the main non-recurring items are the 2 bps IT refund interest benefit and the opportunistic, non-normal CIB quarterly pace (about 6% QoQ), which will not repeat at the same rate.
